vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 Senate votes, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 31. Nay or No: 9. Not Voting: 0. said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text: China uses advanced U.S. AI technology to bolster its cyber, surveillance, fraud, and weapons capabilities. Closing a loophole that allows geopolitical adversaries to remotely access our AI chips is a good step to help ensure our national security and competitive advantage. https://t.co/e8D8HnCpny
https://t.co/w9xIu9cLp6 https://t.co/WM1vHDUiwu
My highs and lows this week: https://t.co/B76C5IRvOG
We need to close loopholes in export controls for advanced AI chips.https://t.co/7FOY6oGOL8

The U.S. should be promoting our competitive edge in AI through reasonable innovation and regulation, not by enabling our strategic adversaries to embrace risky behaviors with these technologies or to acquire them through nefarious means.

Jensen Huang’s gross negligence exposed cracks in our national security, but Secretary Lutnick’s reported stalling on export controls raises the question of whether the Commerce Department is acting in the best interests of the American people. We need answers and accountability from both immediately.

Right now, $25 billion worth of Utah projects are stuck in the federal permitting process. Across the country, the problem is even greater. Getting the bipartisan permitting bill into law will help cut unnecessary delays and ensure important projects can move forward. https://t.co/mBEMgStZqT

Our freedoms were not simply handed to us. They were defended by generations of brave Americans willing to sacrifice for something greater than themselves.

Today, may we honor their sacrifices by being good stewards of the freedoms they defended and by ensuring future generations understand the price of that liberty.

Executive orders may provide a temporary win for one side, but they clearly don’t provide the lasting, consensus-based solution that legislation does. We resolved public land disputes in Emery County through legislation, and with the right level of support, we can do it again in this region too.

Proud to see our bipartisan data center community empowerment legislation included in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. This will ensure local leaders have the clear information they need to make informed decisions for their residents.

Enjoyed bringing together local leaders and stakeholders for roundtable discussions on how we can expand housing opportunities, plan for long-term water needs, and ensure Utah is a place where future generations thrive.

Our pioneer ancestors didn’t let seemingly impossible challenges stand in their way. They found innovative ways to move water in the desert and build thriving communities. Saving the Great Salt Lake will require that same kind of bold thinking. https://t.co/2b2i3POWNF
https://t.co/3emz6XgFMO

There's no doubt that conservation is critical, but it won't be enough to save the Great Salt Lake. Enjoyed speaking with @gopTODD and @UUtah students during the @SutherlandInst's Congressional Series about all that is at stake regarding the lake, and the bold solutions that will be required to maintain its vitality for generations.

Protecting the Great Salt Lake is both an environmental and economic priority, and we need out-of-the-box innovation and strong collaboration to make it happen. It won’t be easy, but Utahns have never been afraid of a challenge.

Listen to our conversation on Deseret Voices here: https://t.co/EUCRYAMgca
The world is a better, freer place when America leads from a position of both strength and moral resolve. https://t.co/LMgHgLdfXR https://t.co/fgJ7MZYuZ2

Looking forward to speaking at today’s @SutherlandInst Congressional Series. If you aren’t able to join in person, tune in here at 1:30 PM MT / 3:30 PM ET:

https://t.co/SoyktlN33N

Highs and lows coming to you from an advanced nuclear reactor site, where I’ve joined senators and governors from the Mountain West to see firsthand how American innovation is paving the way for an affordable, reliable, and clean energy future. https://t.co/ld0FySUozu

Wildfire technology is advancing quickly, but getting the best tools into the hands of firefighters can still take far too long. I appreciated speaking at the Wildfire Technology Summit to discuss how the Fix Our Forests Act can modernize that process, improve wildfire intelligence and coordination, and make sure firefighters have the technology they need to protect themselves and our communities.

In Utah, nearly all of our water supply depends on mountain snowpack. With water being one of the defining challenges facing the West, better forecasting means better decisions for our farmers, communities, and water managers. Proud to see our bipartisan legislation to improve snowpack monitoring and give Western states the information they need to plan ahead pass the Senate.

https://t.co/gV7VGVG9eV

More and more businesses are making major investments in Utah—providing good jobs and supporting local economies. It was great to tour new cutting-edge facilities in Juab County, and discuss how we can remove burdensome, unnecessary regulations and ensure more regulatory predictability from Washington.

Growth, water, and housing affordability are top of mind for Utahns—particularly in communities like Nephi, Manti, and Ephraim. Great to meet with commissioners from Sanpete and Juab Counties, as well as Ephraim Mayor Chris Larsen and members of the city council for a discussion on transportation, business development, and the work we’ve done to improve water infrastructure in the region.
This is the right move, both for the loved ones of the victims and for the country. https://t.co/g6zH0RwAqH

Utah is home to thousands of veteran-owned businesses—many of which play a critical role in supporting our defense industrial base. Enjoyed touring Straight Jacket Armory, which recently set up shop in Nephi, to see how they are supporting various U.S. military units, including Special Operations Forces and Navy SEAL programs.

Utah’s pro-business environment continues to invite large investments that support economic growth and bring jobs to our rural communities. Great touring Nortonville Rail’s steel processing center in Nephi to see firsthand Utah-grown innovation in steel manufacturing. https://t.co/kaHTzKA1Um
Read more: https://t.co/uSPtsdFe9n

Protecting communities from catastrophic wildfires requires more than just fighting fires once they start. We need experts from every field working together to develop innovative, cost-effective solutions. Great to sit down with wildfire experts and Utah leaders to discuss better forest management, wildfire prevention, and recovery efforts that will help our communities prepare for future fires.

Government regulations can disproportionately burden small businesses, which represent 99% of companies in Utah. It’s critical that the regulatory environment is productive, targeted, and efficient. Great to be with the Intermountain Business Alliance to share an update from Washington and learn from our business community.

American manufacturers shouldn't have to navigate conflicting rules on recycled materials. My Recycled Materials Attribution Act would establish clear standards, protect consumers from misleading claims, and give businesses certainty to invest in new recycling innovations.

I commend the Administration for taking the allegations involving Ambassador Guilfoyle seriously. Public service is a public trust, and political connections should never put anyone above accountability. I appreciate President Trump’s willingness to act. That's the kind of leadership Americans are yearning for.

Read more

Utah continues to play a leading role in advancing global health through research, innovation, and humanitarian work. Appreciated joining leaders at the University of Utah to discuss the future of global health, including the threats that the burgeoning national debt poses to economic stability and our ability to help.

Utah’s aerospace and defense industry is vital to our national security. Enjoyed touring ES3’s Clearfield facilities and meeting with employees whose work supports Hill Air Force Base and keeps our military mission-ready. https://t.co/bRzscTx7ZW

Seneca warned that Rome’s bloody spectacles corrupted the people who watched them. A civilization erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment.

Secretary Hegseth’s plan to livestream the Fort Hood execution risks feeding that appetite. The victims deserve justice administered with solemnity. Broadcasting a death diminishes us and is not an effective deterrent. I urge him to reconsider.
